svg.text: PERMANENT rail — BusBoard ST1 stripboard · 3 strips (A B C) · M2 holes on row C, cols 15 and 30
PERMANENT rail — BusBoard ST1 stripboard · 3 strips (A B C) · M2 holes on row C, cols 15 and 30
The copper STRIPS are the buses — nothing across the back, which is what leaves room for the two mounting holes. Both holes are INSIDE the three strips the rail uses.
The copper STRIPS are the buses — nothing across the back, which is what leaves room for the two mounting holes. Both holes are INSIDE the three strips the rail uses.
Row A: 13.8 V (1–12) · SDA (23–27). Row B: GND-power (1–13) · GND-LOGIC (15–20) · SCL (23–27). Row C: GND-LOGIC (1–14) · 3V3 (18–27) — and the two M2 holes, in its DEAD segments.
Row A: 13.8 V (1–12) · SDA (23–27). Row B: GND-power (1–13) · GND-LOGIC (15–20) · SCL (23–27). Row C: GND-LOGIC (1–14) · 3V3 (18–27) — and the two M2 holes, in its DEAD segments.

FIVE track cuts per rail: row A col 17 · row B col 14 (the STAR-GROUND cut) · row B col 21 · row C col 17 and col 28. Meter every cut — a partial cut that still conducts is the failure this method invites.

Only TWO connectors on the whole build are JST-XH, and both are on rail #1: they are the ones that penetrate the sidewall. Everything else is 0.1″ berg. PWR OUT / PWR IN / PACK PWR are 3-pin as of 2026-09-23 — the third contact is GND-logic.

RAIL #2 (PERMANENT, ST1 stripboard) — same board, same buses, same FIVE cuts, NO outward connectors, all berg

6× driver, two 6-pin berg strips, rows A+B, cols 1-6

Rail #2 has no sidewall penetration at all, so every connector on it is berg. PCA9685 and TMP102 keep separate power and I²C taps — and they are the ONLY two loads on GND-logic. The 6 drivers and the fan return on GND-power.

Board: BusBoard ST1 — 31 × 19 holes, 19 strips, tracks along the 31-hole axis. 50 × 80 mm FR4, 1.6 mm, SINGLE-SIDED, 1 oz copper. Datasheet: docs/datasheets/BPS-DAT-ST1-Datasheet.pdf
Board: BusBoard ST1 — 31 × 19 holes, 19 strips, tracks along the 31-hole axis. 50 × 80 mm FR4, 1.6 mm, SINGLE-SIDED, 1 oz copper. Datasheet: docs/datasheets/BPS-DAT-ST1-Datasheet.pdf

ONE board makes BOTH rails. Cut two rails 6 strips wide (15.24 × 80 mm) from strips 3-8 and 11-16. Strips 1-2, 9-10 and 17-19 are waste — the four factory 0.125″ holes sit on strips 2 and 18, so they are cut away.

ONE board makes BOTH rails. Cut two rails 6 strips wide (15.24 × 80 mm) from strips 3-8 and 11-16. Strips 1-2, 9-10 and 17-19 are waste — the four factory 0.125″ holes sit on strips 2 and 18, so they are cut away.

Strip order across a rail: spare · A · B · C · spare · spare. Only A, B and C carry copper that matters. The two spares outboard of C are mechanical only — they give the Ø7 post 6.35 mm of board past the hole centre instead of 1.27 mm.

Strip order across a rail: spare · A · B · C · spare · spare. Only A, B and C carry copper that matters. The two spares outboard of C are mechanical only — they give the Ø7 post 6.35 mm of board past the hole centre instead of 1.27 mm.

SINGLE-SIDED matters: copper is on ONE face. Connector BODIES go on the bare INNER face, leads through, solder on the copper OUTER face — the same face rule as the old rail, so nothing about the harness changes.

SINGLE-SIDED matters: copper is on ONE face. Connector BODIES go on the bare INNER face, leads through, solder on the copper OUTER face — the same face rule as the old rail, so nothing about the harness changes.
The six driver landings are TWO 6-pin berg strips, not six 2-pin headers.
The six driver landings are TWO 6-pin berg strips, not six 2-pin headers.

One 6-pin strip along row A cols 1-6 and another along row B cols 1-6. Every column then offers an A pin and a B pin 2.54 mm apart — exactly what a 2-pin Dupont female plugs onto. Two parts instead of six, and the drivers

One 6-pin strip along row A cols 1-6 and another along row B cols 1-6. Every column then offers an A pin and a B pin 2.54 mm apart — exactly what a 2-pin Dupont female plugs onto. Two parts instead of six, and the drivers
land at 1-column pitch instead of the 3-column cadence a JST-XH body forces. That compression is what buys the room for everything else on the board.

Mounting: two M2 holes ON ROW C at cols 15 and 30 — 15 columns = 38.10 mm apart. Inside the three strips the rail uses. There is no fourth row.
Mounting: two M2 holes ON ROW C at cols 15 and 30 — 15 columns = 38.10 mm apart. Inside the three strips the rail uses. There is no fourth row.

The ONLY electrical constraint on a mounting hole is that drilling SEVERS the strip it is in. The post is printed plastic and the screw head lands on the bare inner face, so nothing can short — a Ø2.2 hole in a ~2 mm track

simply cuts it. So the hole only has to sit where severing the strip costs nothing. Row C now carries GND-logic on cols 1-14 and 3V3 on 18-27, cut at 17 and 28 — which leaves cols 15-16 and 29-31 dead. Cols 15 and 30 fall inside those
dead segments, so they cost NO extra cuts — the same four cuts do both jobs. Rows A and B have no dead segment: with one cut each, every part of those strips belongs to one of their two nets.

Col 30, not 29: a Ø2.2 hole at col 29 would merge with the row-C cut at col 28 (−0.06 mm of material between them). Col 30 leaves 2.48 mm to the cut and 3.34 mm to the board end.

Drill the existing Ø0.94 holes out to Ø2.2. Cols 15 and 30 and their neighbours are connector-free on BOTH rails, so the Ø7 post seats on bare board and never lands on a solder joint. The post reaches 3.5 mm, so it also

Drill the existing Ø0.94 holes out to Ø2.2. Cols 15 and 30 and their neighbours are connector-free on BOTH rails, so the Ø7 post seats on bare board and never lands on a solder joint. The post reaches 3.5 mm, so it also

covers row B at cols 14-16 and 29-31 — pin-free there on both rails — and does not reach row A at all (5.08 mm away). CAD: RAIL_POST_Z 42.5 / 80.0 → 42.5 / 80.6, so the posts are exactly 15 columns apart.

That was wrong twice over: it widened the rail to 17.78 mm for no reason, and it was solving a short that cannot happen. Nothing shorts through a plastic post. The holes belong in the three strips already in use.

That was wrong twice over: it widened the rail to 17.78 mm for no reason, and it was solving a short that cannot happen. Nothing shorts through a plastic post. The holes belong in the three strips already in use.
Why this replaces the bare-wire perfboard rail.
Why this replaces the bare-wire perfboard rail.

That design soldered five bare buses into every hole along the back of the board. It worked, but the back was then wall-to-wall solder and every column had a live wire crossing it — so a drilled hole always cut a bus.

That design soldered five bare buses into every hole along the back of the board. It worked, but the back was then wall-to-wall solder and every column had a live wire crossing it — so a drilled hole always cut a bus.

On stripboard the buses are etched copper, the back carries only joints, and five track cuts plus one short link replace five hand-laid wires. Those same cuts create the dead row-C segments the mounting holes sit in.

On stripboard the buses are etched copper, the back carries only joints, and five track cuts plus one short link replace five hand-laid wires. Those same cuts create the dead row-C segments the mounting holes sit in.
[X] The India stopgap rail is CANCELLED (2026-09-23) and its boards were thrown away. This stripboard design is the USA build.
